# Reproducibility

This closing chapter gives a reader everything needed to trust the numbers in
this guide and to rerun them: the software environment, the seeds that make the
runs deterministic, a map from each paper output to the script that produces it,
and an inventory of what is shipped. Every figure and table in the guide is
regenerated from these files; nothing is transcribed by hand.

## Environment

The package builds under **R $\ge$ 4.5** and was built and rendered on R 4.6.
The two tracks have different requirements:

- **Track A** (from-scratch: simulation plus the restricted-data application)
  needs **CmdStan $\ge$ 2.35** through the `cmdstanr` interface and the
  `svyder` package, because it fits the Stan models and calls the production
  diagnostic API.
- **Track B** (regenerate every figure and table from the shipped results) and
  **this book** need **neither Stan, `svyder`, nor the restricted data**. Track
  B reads precomputed `.rds` files and fits nothing.

The production Design Effect Ratio implementation lives in the
[`svyder`](https://github.com/joonho112/svyder) package, which Track A calls
directly. The files under `code/helpers/` are **self-contained ports of the same
computations**, so the replication does not depend on a moving upstream package:
it can be pinned on its own and will reproduce even if `svyder` changes. The
setup script `code/00_setup.R` is track-aware: by default it checks the R
version and installs/loads only the CRAN packages needed for Track B reporting
and this book. To prepare the full Track A toolchain, set
`SVYDER_TRACK = "A"` before sourcing the script; that path additionally checks
`cmdstanr`, verifies or installs CmdStan, and installs `svyder` from GitHub.

A live `sessionInfo()` for the environment that rendered this page appears
[at the end of the chapter](#session-information).

## Seeds and determinism

The simulation is fully deterministic. The base seed is **20260704**, and the
helper `get_rep_seed(cell_number, rep_id)` in
`code/01_simulation/sim_00_config.R` assigns each replication its own
non-overlapping stream,

```r
get_rep_seed <- function(cell_number, rep_id, base_seed = 20260704L) {
  as.integer(base_seed + cell_number * 10000L + rep_id)
}
```

Because every replication draws from a seed fixed this way --- and the two
edge-case rules described in the [simulation design](03-simulation-design.qmd)
keep the sampled weights exact --- rerunning Track A reproduces the shipped
replication files **bit-for-bit**, which has been verified. The NSECE fit is
seeded separately, at **20260705**; its four chains, warmup, and `adapt_delta`
are recorded in the fit metadata printed in the
[application chapter](06-application-data.qmd).

## Provenance map

Each paper output is produced by exactly one script. The table below maps them.

| Output | Produced by | Reads from |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Figure 1 (theory curves) | `code/03_results/results_01_theory.R` | closed forms only (no data) |
| Figure 2 (DER separation), Figure 3 (coverage), Table 2 (coverage) | `code/03_results/results_02_aggregate.R` | the simulation shards |
| Figure 4 (NSECE dual-target), Table 3 (dual-target DER), Table 5 (threshold sweep) | `code/03_results/results_02_aggregate.R` | `nsece_v2_refit.rds` |
| Table 4 (weight-convention sensitivity) | `code/03_results/results_02_aggregate.R` | `nsece_v2_refit.rds` + `nsece_supp.rds` |
| The 4,800 simulation shards | `code/01_simulation/sim_05_run_batch.R` (via `sim_04_run_single.R` and stages `sim_00`--`sim_03`) | synthetic data generated internally |
| `nsece_v2_refit.rds` | `code/02_application/app_02_fit_refit.R` | restricted NSECE derivatives |
| `nsece_supp.rds` | `code/02_application/app_03_der_supplement.R` | restricted NSECE derivatives |

Figure 1 is analytic and needs no inputs. The two `results_*` scripts are the
whole of the reporting stage (Track B): they fit no models and read no
restricted data. The simulation shards and the two NSECE result files are their
only inputs, and all three are shipped.

## What is shipped for Track B

Track B runs entirely from files included in the package, all of them
non-identifiable:

- **The 4,800 simulation replication files** under `output/simulation/`, laid
  out as 24 design cells $\times$ 200 replications. Each `rep_XXXX.rds` carries
  the per-replication DER vectors, coverage, and interval widths --- synthetic
  data only.
- **The per-cell simulation summary** under `data/precomputed/simulation/`
  (`simulation_cell_summary.rds`), the aggregated view the figures and tables
  read.
- **The two NSECE result files** under `data/precomputed/application/`:
  `nsece_v2_refit.rds` (posterior draws and dual-target DER results under the
  declared convention) and `nsece_supp.rds` (the weight-convention sensitivity
  and the structural factors).

The **restricted NSECE microdata are never shipped** and never committed. The
result files carry posterior summaries, DER vectors, and scalars --- no
respondent-level record of any kind. See `data/DATA_ACCESS.md` and the
[application chapter](06-application-data.qmd) for the boundary in full.

## A note on the convergence gate

Every fit is held to the same **strict** gate: split-$\widehat{R} \le 1.01$ on
**all** parameters, bulk ESS $\ge 100$, and zero divergent transitions. A
replication that fails any of these is excluded from the summaries.

In the simulation, **33 of the 4,800 replications fail the gate** (a pass rate
of about 99.3%). The failures are excluded from every reported summary but
**retained on disk**, so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent: the
shards are all present under `output/simulation/`, and the per-cell summary
records the fail counts alongside the used counts. The NSECE fit clears the gate
comfortably, at $\widehat{R} \le 1.004$ with no divergences, as the
[application chapter](06-application-data.qmd) shows.

## Where to go next

For the theory --- the definitions, the tier decomposition, the theorems, and
their proofs --- see the paper [@LeeWilliamsSavitsky2026]. For the production
Design Effect Ratio API that Track A calls, and that you would use on your own
survey model, see the [`svyder`](https://github.com/joonho112/svyder)
documentation. This guide has shown how the two studies in the paper are set up,
run, and reduced to the reported numbers; the paper and the package carry it the
rest of the way.
